claims.statement: Verified fact: Polish aggregation combines electricity demand, generation, or storage to sell energy or provide system and flexibility services; URE reported 16 entities in its aggregator list and requires evidence of actual aggregation activity.

Verified fact: EU law explicitly permits dedicated measurement data, with customer consent, for observability and settlement of flexibility services when smart-meter data is absent or insufficiently granular.
Hypothesis (unvalidated): emerging aggregators will outsource baseline, participant revenue allocation, and dispute evidence rather than treat all settlement as a core internal capability.

contrary_evidence: Only 16 entities were in URE's aggregator list at the cited date, indicating a potentially small and immature immediate customer pool: https://www.ure.gov.pl/pl/urzad/informacje-ogolne/aktualnosci/12810%2CTransformacja-energetyczna-16-podmiotow-w-wykazie-agregatorow.html
EU baseline methodologies and financial-settlement principles are still being specified, creating rule-change risk: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/C/2025/3699

economics.acquisition_route: Partner with one battery/EMS integrator and run parallel shadow settlement for a registered aggregator without touching market bids or funds.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Unvalidated scenario: 4 portfolios at PLN 10,000 MRR in year 2, 18 at PLN 16,000 MRR in year 4, and 30 at PLN 20,000 MRR in year 6 imply PLN 7.2m ARR before activation fees. At a 3-5x infrastructure-software value and 55% ownership, PLN 5m net worth is plausible in years 5-7; if baseline disputes cannot be reduced across two asset classes, the thesis fails.
economics.founder_time: 4-5 hours/day for one asset class and one aggregator; keep market operations, 24/7 control, and licensing outside scope.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Hypothesis: 78-90% for automated settlement; meter remediation and disputes must be separately bounded.
economics.payback: Unvalidated customer hypothesis: fewer participant disputes and faster revenue allocation repay the platform within 6-12 months; compare shadow and production statements.
economics.pricing: Unvalidated estimate: PLN 3,000-15,000 monthly per portfolio plus PLN 10-60 per settled activation or 0.5-2% of revenue administered, subject to legal review.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Every activation and settlement period repeats; participant contracts and historical baselines make switching costly.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: event histories improve baseline diagnostics and asset reliability estimates; contractual rule and meter mappings create durable workflow lock-in
fingerprint.customer: Polish independent aggregators, energy-service firms, and commercial battery or flexible-load portfolio owners
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: battery and energy-management integrators, meter-data vendors, and a shadow-settlement pilot with a registered aggregator
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: meter/dispatch ingestion, versioned baseline engine, event replay, revenue-share and imbalance allocation, participant statement, and dispute evidence API
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: aggregator or portfolio owner pays per MW/site-month and per settled activation when participant statements close
fingerprint.problem_trigger: a dispatch event or settlement period ends and the aggregator must prove delivered flexibility and allocate market revenue and imbalance adjustments to participating sites

founder_fit: Counterfactual modeling, time-series data, and uncertainty quantification are strong founder matches.
Family renewable-energy context can help source asset-domain understanding without operating the market.
B2B technical channels avoid camera-led consumer acquisition.
A shadow settlement can validate safely while the founder remains employed.
risks: Baseline choice is contentious and can materially redistribute revenue.
Meter quality and customer consent may be inadequate.
Market rules and the EU demand-response network code are evolving.
Aggregators may regard settlement logic as core intellectual property and build it themselves.

structure.commercial_archetype: market-service baseline and revenue settlement agent
structure.control_point: agreed baseline-to-meter calculation that allocates a flexibility event's delivered volume, revenue, and imbalance cost across assets
structure.critical_dependency: high-granularity interval meter and dispatch data plus an aggregator contract that defines baseline and revenue-allocation rules

thesis: Sell aggregators and owners of batteries, EV charging, refrigeration, or controllable industrial loads a neutral settlement service that reconstructs the counterfactual baseline, binds dispatch instructions to interval meter data, calculates delivered flexibility, attributes revenue and imbalance costs to sites, and produces a dispute-ready statement. It does not aggregate or trade energy initially; the aggregator pays per settled portfolio and retains market responsibility.
title: Behind-the-Meter Flexibility Settlement Agent
uncertainties: Polish activation volume and addressable third-party settlement spend are unknown.
The best first asset class and baseline method require partner data.
Whether revenue-share pricing creates regulated or agency obligations needs counsel.
It is unproven that neutrality matters enough to overcome aggregator integration friction.
